prompt: Put in order what happens between your click and the line a recorder saves, and then the replay.
items: The recorder's script in the page hears the click
The locator builder picks the first name that finds that element alone
A step is saved: command, target, value
On replay, the target is looked up again and the command repeated
trap: The name is chosen while you record, not while the test replays; that is why it can be wrong on the next load.

prompt: You record: open the shop, add a banana, add a mango, assert the count says 2. Which of these is missing from the saved recording?

choices.text: The target the builder chose for each click
choices.why: Every click is saved with the target the builder chose; that is the middle move.

choices.text: That the basket must start empty
choices.why: Right. The shop happened to be empty when you recorded; emptying it was never a click, so nothing records it.

choices.text: The value 2 the assertion compares with
choices.why: You asked for the assertion from a menu, and its value is saved with it.

choices.text: The address the recording started at
choices.why: A `.side` file keeps it in `url`, and codegen writes it into `goto`.

prompt: A recording passed on the afternoon it was made. The next morning it fails on its first click, and the page looks exactly the same. What is the likeliest reason?

choices.text: The replay is too fast for the button to appear
choices.why: Both replays shown in this lesson wait for the target before clicking; a missing wait would fail on a fresh page too, not only the next day.

choices.text: The browser kept yesterday's page in its cache
choices.why: A replay opens a fresh browser profile; and a cached page would still draw the same button.

choices.text: Its saved name uses a value redrawn each load
choices.why: Right. A name such as `#card-4821` was true while recording and is another number on every load since.

choices.text: The recorder lost some of the events overnight
choices.why: A saved recording is a file; nothing in it changes by itself.

prompt: What is a Selenium IDE `.side` file?

choices.text: A video of the browser while you recorded
choices.why: Nothing visual is kept; the file is text.

choices.text: A Java program the IDE compiled from your clicks
choices.why: Code is something the export packages produce on request; the recording itself is data.

choices.text: JSON: tests made of commands and targets
choices.why: Right. `side-model` declares it: project, tests, commands with `command`, `target`, `targets` and `value`, and suites that name tests by id.

choices.text: The settings of a grid
choices.why: Grids belong to lesson 8; a `.side` file holds recordings.

prompt: Match each of the IDE's locator builders to the target it gives on the shop.
Without the `pause`, the IDE's replay of the recording fails on `assertText` although the shop works. Why, by the playback code?

choices.text: It reads the text once, maybe before it changed
choices.why: Right. It waits for the element to exist, reads once and compares; a `0` at that instant is a failure.

choices.text: It tried a fallback target and found another span
choices.why: The loop that would try `targets` is commented out; only `target` is used.

choices.text: Its clicks do not wait for their button at all
choices.why: A click polls for up to the implicit wait, five seconds by default.

choices.text: It compares `2` with the total instead of the count
choices.why: The target names the count by its `data-testid`; the element is right, the moment is wrong.

prompt: The same recording named the count well and the banana's button badly. What made the difference?

choices.text: The count lives in the header, which never changes
choices.why: The builders do not ask where an element lives; they ask what it carries.

choices.text: The IDE looks for `data-testid` before anything else, and the button lacks it
choices.why: The first builder looks for `data-test-id` and `data-test`; `data-testid` is taken by the third.

choices.text: The count has a `data-*` attribute; the button needs a parent's id
choices.why: Right. `css:data-attr` names the count; the button has none of its own, so `css:finder` climbs to the card's random id.

choices.text: XPath is used for buttons, CSS for text
choices.why: The order is the same for every element; CSS came first for both.

prompt: A BugBug suite with automatic retries has been green all week. What should a tester look at before trusting it?

choices.text: The schedule, to check it ran every five minutes
choices.why: A run that happened tells you nothing about whether it passed first time.

choices.text: The run history, for the attempts it marked auto-retried
choices.why: Right. A pass on a retry turns the suite green and hides a flaky test, which is lesson 14's warning.

choices.text: The price of the plan
choices.why: The plan decides what you may run, not whether the runs mean anything.

choices.text: The extension's incognito setting
choices.why: That matters while recording; the question is about runs in the service.

prompt: Which of these is a risk of keeping tests in a hosted service, and not in your repository?

choices.text: A change to a test is not reviewed with the change to the app
choices.why: Right. The two travel separately, so nobody reads them side by side in one pull request.

choices.text: The service cannot take a screenshot of the page when a test fails
choices.why: Ghost Inspector's documentation describes screenshot comparison; pictures are what these services do well.

choices.text: Its tests are slower than tests on your laptop
choices.why: Nothing in this lesson measured that, and speed is not what the model gives up.

choices.text: Its recordings never run on a schedule
choices.why: Schedules are the headline feature of both services.

prompt: What does `PWDEBUG=console` add to the pages Playwright opens?

choices.text: A window called the Inspector, beside the browser
choices.why: That is codegen, and it needs a screen; the console mode ran headless here.

choices.text: A `playwright` object with `generateLocator`
choices.why: Right. `pick.mjs` called it on twelve elements to see the names codegen would write.

choices.text: A log of every request the page makes, in the terminal
choices.why: That is the shop's `QUITANDA_LOG=1`, on the server's side.

choices.text: A slower page, so that every action can be watched
choices.why: Slowing actions down is `slowMo`, a launch option, not this variable.

prompt: The generator named the shop's total `getByText('R$ 0,00')`. What goes wrong in a test that uses that name?

choices.text: The space after R$ is not a normal space, so it never matches
choices.why: Locators by text treat any run of whitespace as one space, as lesson 2 showed; the name matched while the total was zero.

choices.text: It matches all eight prices
choices.why: No product costs R$ 0,00; the name was unique, which is why the generator chose it.

choices.text: It finds nothing once anything is in the basket
choices.why: Right. The element was named by the value it had, and its job is to change; after a banana it says R$ 5,90.

choices.text: `getByText` cannot be used inside a test file
choices.why: It is one of the locators lesson 2 listed; the problem is the text chosen.

prompt: To make codegen write Python with pytest, you run `npx playwright codegen --___ python-pytest`.
hint: The option that chooses the language, from the `--help` output.

prompt: A colleague's codegen recording clicks the Pineapple with `locator('#card-4126 > button')`. It passed when recorded. What do you do with that line?

choices.text: Record the session again until a better name comes out
choices.why: The generator gave the same kind of name on both runs of `pick.mjs`; recording again draws only a new number.

choices.text: Keep it, because it passed when it was made
choices.why: It passed on the one load whose number it copied; `acerola` in `codegen.spec.js` failed the same way.

choices.text: Add `waitForTimeout(2000)` before the click
choices.why: Waiting longer for an element that has another id never finds it.

choices.text: Use the card's test id and the button's role and name instead
choices.why: Right. That is the name the generator gave the other six buttons, and it does not depend on the load.

prompt: `recorded/side.spec.js` stopped on its first click. For how many milliseconds did that click wait, by the timeout in the message?
hint: The same as the IDE's implicit wait by default.

prompt: In `recorded/codegen.spec.js`, `two fruit` passed, and afterwards the basket held two bananas and a mango. How did its check pass?

choices.text: The mango's click was lost, so the count stopped at 2
choices.why: The basket shows the mango arrived; the count went on to 3.

choices.text: `toContainText('2')` saw the 2 on the way from 1 to 3
choices.why: Right. The first test's banana was left over; the assertion keeps asking, and a passing moment of `2` was enough.

choices.text: The fixture emptied the basket before the test
choices.why: A recording uses the plain `page`; there is no fixture and no reset in it.

choices.text: Two workers shared out the clicks between them
choices.why: The recordings ran one after another in one worker, which is exactly how the banana stayed.

prompt: Why does this lesson keep the recordings in `recorded/` with their own configuration, rather than marking them `test.fail()` in `tests/`?

choices.text: Because `test.fail()` cannot be used in a file Playwright generated
choices.why: A recording is an ordinary test file once saved; anything can be added to it.

choices.text: Because the separate folder makes the recordings run faster
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it; the folder decides what a plain run reads.

choices.text: Because one of them passes, and there is no shop defect to document
choices.why: Right. `test.fail()` would turn the banana test's pass red, and it exists to document a defect in the app, not in the test.

choices.text: Because lesson 14 forbids tests that fail
choices.why: Lesson 14 keeps flaky tests apart; it does not forbid keeping a failure to study.

prompt: After the button's words changed, how many lines of `recorded/codegen.spec.js` named the old words and had to be edited?
Both the recording and the page-object tests failed after *Add to basket* became *Add to cart*. Why is that no argument against locating by role and name?

choices.text: Because the failure was caused by the shared basket
choices.why: The run used one worker and the fixture resets; every failure waited for the button by its old name.

choices.text: Because a locator by position would have failed too
choices.why: It would not have: the order did not change. That is lesson 2's other way to be wrong, passing on the wrong thing.

choices.text: Because the words a customer reads did change
choices.why: Right. A test by role and name ought to look again then; the difference between the two sides is the cost of the fix, one line against three.

choices.text: Because role locators ignore the text of a button
choices.why: The name of a button is its text; that is why the change reached them.

prompt: Which of these is a use of a recorder this lesson calls fine?

choices.text: The regression suite the team keeps for years
choices.why: A test that has to live is where every cost counted here keeps being paid.

choices.text: The tests that gate a merge in CI
choices.why: A gate has to be trusted, and a recording starts from whatever state it finds.

choices.text: A reproduction for a defect report
choices.why: Right. It is deleted with the defect, so nobody maintains it and its weaknesses cost nothing.

choices.text: The checks of a page whose words change every week
choices.why: That is where the count of edits grows fastest.

prompt: Put in order what happened when `recorded/side.spec.js` ran.
items: The shop opened and the window was resized
The first click looked for `#card-4821 > button`
Five seconds passed with no such element
The test failed before the pause and the check ran

prompt: A team has 200 recorded flows in a hosted service, and a designer renames the *Checkout* button to *Pay now*. What should the team expect?

choices.text: Nothing, because the service stores a screenshot of each button
choices.why: A screenshot comparison would add failures, not prevent them; the steps still name the button.

choices.text: Every flow naming it by its words fails
choices.why: Right. Each is then edited by hand: a recording repeats a name once per click that used it, and there is no single place to change it.

choices.text: One failure, since the service deduplicates identical steps
choices.why: Nothing in either service's documentation describes merging steps across tests.

choices.text: Only the flows on the schedule fail
choices.why: A schedule decides when a test runs, not whether its locator still matches.
